evidence.claim: Every enumerated stage is mapped to the provider clause it touches, with the clause quoted and dated 2026-08-24.

Default enablement was measured by an isolated HOME, a marketplace install that placed no files, and a worktree census: no MCP config is active after that fresh install, and no live restricted stage is default-on.
The deliverable separates restricted-and-default-on (release blocker) from restricted-and-opt-in-with-documented-warning (acceptable) from unrestricted. A flat list of concerns is not the result.
Catalog reviewer_requirement asks for a cross-vendor refuter PLUS explicit owner sign-off. Neither a second-vendor Codex session nor an owner attestation is on this worktree.

probes.raw_output: reviewer_requirement=one cross-vendor refuter PLUS explicit owner sign-off

evidence.settling_experiment: Dispatch a cross-vendor refute on the raw probes and record an owner_signoff digest on any remaining live blocker.

negative_controls.description: A synthetic install that enables scrape-of-provider-surface plus shared plaintext keys plus 429-retry-with-no-backoff must be classified restricted-and-default-on. A classifier that labels everything unrestricted is a no-op.
blueprint.customer-council.compose is pure-compute with no provider. It must stay unrestricted so a detector that flags every stage is over-broad.

report.answer: On this worktree search-hub is present at tools/mcp/search-hub and fronts official Exa/Tavily/Firecrawl/SearXNG APIs; a 429 does not cool or rotate keys. Isolated-HOME plus an unsigned marketplace install activated no MCP config, so no live stage is restricted-and-default-on. Planted control planted.restricted-default-on is restricted-and-default-on (release blocker). Planted control planted.restricted-opt-in-warned is restricted-and-opt-in-with-documented-warning. Live local reducers, marketplace installer, CNF vendor oracles, and catalog-declared official-API stages that are not default-on are unrestricted. Live release blockers=none. SUCCESS:ADV-0053
